name: wispr-flow-text-animation

frames.best_why: The loop has been reshaped with blue anchors and handles visible while the text still follows the new curve.

tagline: A paragraph streams endlessly along a looping curve you can reshape.
summary: A block of spoken-style text marches continuously along a bezier curve across a dark screen. Edit path reveals draggable anchors and handles that bend the curve live while the text keeps flowing.
appearance: A black full-bleed field with a small grey paragraph wrapped along a thin winding line: a long sweep from the upper left, a tight loop near the centre, then a run to the lower right. A tiny pill at the top centre reads Edit path.
behaviour: The paragraph scrolls steadily along the curve in an endless loop. Pressing Edit path shows a blue dashed outline, anchor dots and hollow control handles; dragging them reshapes the curve while the text follows, and Done editing returns to the plain view.
demo_content: A long rambling quote about a project timeline, starting Umm, hope your week has started well
search_phrases: text flowing along a curved line
voice transcript flowing across the screen
drag points to bend the text path
use_when: A launch or landing screen wants a wall of speech-like copy drifting on a curve that can be art-directed live.
avoid_when: Anywhere the text must be read: it is small, faint and always moving, and it needs a wide screen.
customise: Speed, font size, text opacity and colours are props, but the paragraph is a constant. The curve can be reshaped in edit mode but that shape is not saved.
weight_why: One SVG text path and a short SMIL marquee; only the edit buttons animate with motion.

a11y.note: Path editing is pointer-only, the anchor dots cannot be focused, and the marquee runs regardless of reduced-motion.

issues: The moving text is tiny and very faint, so most of the paragraph cannot be read.
The path handles are small circles with no keyboard focus or labels.
polish_why: Distinctive flowing type with a robust path editor; faint small text holds it back.
